R181.note: Moves ownerId spread after extraCriteria so it can't be overridden; _id can still be overridden by extra but ownerId still constrains the query so no cross-user leak.

R182.note: jwt.NewParser(WithValidMethods) + ParseWithClaims with &jwt.MapClaims{} is correct golang-jwt/v5 usage; blocks alg-confusion/none and the claims pointer assertion matches what was passed in.

R183.note: redis-py client with HSET via mapping replaces raw RESP-unframed socket writes; each field/value is framed separately, closing CRLF command injection while preserving the HSET semantics.

R184.note: Resolve-then-normalize-then-startsWith is the canonical fix; Path.startsWith compares path components so it also avoids the sibling-directory string-prefix trap. Matches contract exactly.

R185.note: URI host/scheme check correctly rejects external hosts, scheme-relative //host, and javascript:/data: while allowing relative paths; standard open-redirect mitigation.

R186.note: Allowlist of diagnostic tool names closes exec.Command executable-name injection; restriction to known tools is disclosed as the intended behavior.

R187.note: Adds separator-boundary check (equal or prefix+separator) which correctly defeats the uploads/uploads-backup sibling-directory string-prefix bypass while still allowing legitimate files under uploadsDir.

R188.note: text() with bindparams/execute dict parameterization is the correct SQLAlchemy fix; query shape and result handling unchanged.

R189.note: strnlen(name, sizeof(name)) returns the existing length for NUL-containing names, bounds at 16 for unterminated ones, and never touches flags. Matches contract.

R190.note: Parameterized JNDI search({0} placeholder + filterArgs) is the correct RFC4515-safe API; preserves the two-clause filter and street literal.

R191.note: random_bytes(32)/bin2hex replaces attacker-seedable mt_rand; token format changes (hex string vs numeric) is an inherent, disclosed part of using a real CSPRNG here.

R192.note: Validates against segment.size() instead of the caller-supplied claimedCapacity, matching the contract's explicit statement that callers no longer need a trustworthy claimed capacity.

R193.note: Adds PasswordEncoder.matches() verification plus a dummy-hash comparison on the not-found/no-password paths to blunt username-enumeration timing; correctly closes the missing credential check.

R194.note: Query builder ->where('region', $region) parameterizes the value; JSON output shape unchanged (Collection is Arrayable/JsonSerializable same as the prior array).

R195.note: PreparedStatement with setString(1, param) is the standard fix; query structure and insert semantics unchanged.

R196.note: JexlSandbox(false) is confirmed (Apache docs) to be deny-by-default ('block-box'); allow(ReportRow) permits only its getters, so amount/region/owner comparisons and row getters keep working while Runtime-style calls are blocked.

R197.note: OrderSecurity.isOwner() calls order.getOwnerId(), but the real Order entity (Order.java) has no such method/field - only getCustomerUsername(). The fix as written will not compile, silently breaking the endpoint.

R198.note: escapeHtml() applied to the injected note before template interpolation correctly closes the reflected XSS; other interpolated fields are non-attacker-controlled.

R199.note: Allowlisting extraCriteria to only the documented 'status' key (per the route's own comment) closes the ownerId-override/authorization bypass entirely; the one narrowing of scope is stated openly and matches documented usage.

R200.note: tika.detect(Path) reads file bytes instead of trusting the client-preserved extension; rewrite matches the real controller's fields/constants and adds a validated-extension mapping, closing the extension-spoofing gap.

R201.note: Bounds-checks payloadLength against frameBuffer.size() before memcpy; returns false instead of reading out of bounds, preserving the function's existing success/failure contract.

R202.note: Removes the SignatureValidator override that returned an unverified JsonWebToken; default JwtBearer validation (via Authority) resumes doing real signature checks. Minimal, correct deletion.

R203.note: Argument-list subprocess.run without shell=True closes metacharacter injection; input_path is always prefixed by UPLOAD_DIR so it can't itself start with '-', avoiding the usual argv-array option-injection gap. Added filename validation is disclosed.

R204.note: Parameterized DirContext.search with {0} filterExpr/filterArgs is the correct RFC4515-safe API, consistent with sibling LDAP entries.

R205.note: Swaps java.util.Random for SecureRandom in the same nextFloat()/substring pattern; matches the standard OWASP-Benchmark-style remediation for this CWE-330 case.

R206.note: sanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, rawBody) is Angular's correct safe replacement for bypassSecurityTrustHtml(); it strips script vectors while preserving allowed tags like <b>/<em>/<a>, matching the contract.

R207.note: crypto.randomBytes(12).toString('hex') is the right API, but the shown fix snippet declares 'const crypto = require("crypto")' twice in the same scope - pasted literally it is a SyntaxError (duplicate declaration).

R208.note: Parameterized DirContext.search with filterArgs closes the LDAP filter injection; consistent with the other Case-series LDAP entries.

R209.note: pool.execute(sql, [userId], cb) with a '?' placeholder is mysql2's correct parameterized API, replacing template-literal interpolation; result shape unchanged.

R210.note: InternetAddress strict validation plus Jakarta Mail Transport.send correctly blocks CRLF envelope injection, but the rewrite silently changes the email body (subjectLine becomes a real Subject header instead of the body content) and adds mail.smtp.starttls.required=true, which could break delivery against a relay that doesn't support STARTTLS - both disclosed only vaguely, and the explanation's 'maintaining the same functional behaviour' claim is inaccurate.

R211.note: Removing @csrf_exempt (and its now-unused import) restores Django's CsrfViewMiddleware token check; the view body is otherwise untouched, matching the stated contract exactly.

R212.note: smtplib.sendmail() routes through putcmd(), which raises ValueError on embedded CR/LF (confirmed against CPython source) - correctly closes the injection; message content and subject/body are preserved.

R213.note: Promotes to long before multiplying and returns 400 on overflow via Math.toIntExact, matching the contract's 'still returns 400 rather than raising' and leaving the length-as-text response untouched.

R214.note: firebase/php-jwt v6 JWT::decode(token, new Key($secret,'HS256')) is the correct signature-verifying API for that version; claims access correctly adapted from array to object, with graceful null fallback preserved.

R215.note: html.escape() on the untrusted text before building the mark_safe'd fragment closes the XSS while the surrounding HTML structure is unchanged.

R216.note: HTML::Entities::encode_entities() on the note parameter is the standard Perl output-encoding fix for this sink; nothing else in the output changes.

R217.note: Scoping get_queryset() to owner=self.request.user matches IsTicketOwner's documented contract and the model (owner FK exists); the staff/assigned_to alternative is explicitly hedged as speculative pending field confirmation, and the model has no such field, so it is correctly not presented as the primary fix.

R218.note: htmlspecialchars() on $message at the final render site covers both the comment and the customerName that was concatenated into it upstream, closing XSS for both taint sources even though the write-up names only comment.

R219.note: Adds the missing $_FILES['avatar']['error'] !== UPLOAD_ERR_OK check before the MIME/move logic, exactly the documented gap; existing checks and flow are otherwise untouched.

R220.note: Structured logging placeholder {Username} instead of string interpolation is ILogger's standard log-forging mitigation; log message content otherwise unchanged.
